first_impression.reaction: Googled '12 month wedding checklist' because I wanted a spreadsheet-able timeline, not a mood board. Jumped to the FAQ first. Straight answers with real numbers: 1 to 18 months for the NOIM, 6 weeks for passports, all from government sources and dated. That's more than most planner blogs give you. Then I hit a Concierge pitch in the third section, before the checklist has even started, and still no word anywhere on what the planner costs or whether they take a cut.

journey.quote: Your Notice of Intended Marriage must reach your authorised celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding.
journey.reaction: An actual number with an actual window. I can check that against the government site in ten seconds.

journey.section: How does a 12 month checklist change for a destination wedding?
journey.quote: Overseas, the paperwork, the passports and your guests' travel all have lead times you cannot shorten by paying more or working late.
journey.reaction: Fair point and not a sales line. Nobody can buy a faster passport.

journey.section: How does a 12 month checklist change for a destination wedding?
journey.quote: If you would rather hand the logistics to one team, Wedded Concierge plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
journey.reaction: Pitch before a single checklist item. And 'payments' again. Do you handle supplier payments, and do you take a margin on them?

journey.section: 12 months out: what to do first
journey.quote: If you are in Australia, lodging a new or renewal application generally cancels your current passport, so you cannot travel on it while you wait.
journey.reaction: Didn't know that. That's the kind of catch I actually want flagged. Useful.

journey.section: 12 months out: what to do first
journey.quote: Agree what you will spend and who is contributing, in writing between the two of you, before any venue conversation.
journey.reaction: Good advice, but the whole article never puts a dollar figure on anything. Not even a rough split of what goes where.

journey.section: 8 to 9 months out: attire, accommodation and the celebrant
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor is the one person who plans with you from start to finish, works in your time zone and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: 'Agrees the fee in writing' is better than nothing. But what is the fee? Flat, percentage, commission from suppliers? That's my first question and it's dodged.

journey.section: 3 months out: trials, fittings and paperwork
journey.quote: As at November 2026, you cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised here if it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law.
journey.reaction: Dated, specific, admits the limitation. This is the tone I trust.

journey.section: Your 12 month wedding checklist at a glance
journey.quote: For a printable version alongside real weddings and destination ideas, sign up for the Wedded Wonderland magazine.
journey.reaction: You just told me to print the table. Now I have to hand over my email for a 'printable version'? Mild bait.

journey.quote: For a small wedding in Australia, it can be, provided your NOIM reaches your celebrant at least 1 month before the wedding.
journey.reaction: Honest answer. Doesn't scare me into hiring someone.

journey.section: Plan the year with one person beside you
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor helps you decide it, as your single point of contact from the first idea, quoting in AUD and confirming inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Quoting in AUD is fine. Still no 'from' price, no commission disclosure, no real wedding with a real budget. Same silence as every planner site.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does a 12 month plan cost in AUD, and how does spend usually split across venue, catering, photography, attire? (sourced figures or 'not published')
How far ahead do destination guests actually need save-the-dates and invitations, in months? The page says 'earlier' but gives no number.
What does a CNI or apostille typically cost and how long does it take?
How is the Wedded Concierge fee calculated, and what's the 'from AUD' figure? (deferred business detail)
Does Wedded Concierge take commission or mark up supplier prices when it handles 'payments'? (deferred business detail)
Is Wonderland Studio your own product, and is it free? (deferred business detail)
Show me a real wedding you planned on this timeline, with the actual budget. (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: If you would rather hand the logistics to one team, Wedded Concierge plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
turn_offs_found.why: CTA before any evidence: it sits above the first checklist block, and 'payments' raises the commission question without answering it.

turn_offs_found.quote: With the venue and date held, turn to the suppliers whose calendars fill first and whose work you will look at for the rest of your life.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional framing where a lead time in months would do the job.

turn_offs_found.quote: A Wedded Advisor is the one person who plans with you from start to finish, works in your time zone and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
turn_offs_found.why: Mentions a fee but gives no model, range or commission disclosure, which is the exact thing I'm comparing planners on.

turn_offs_found.quote: For a printable version alongside real weddings and destination ideas, sign up for the Wedded Wonderland magazine.
turn_offs_found.why: Email gate on a table I was just told to print; feels like a lead-capture trick.

would_share_with: My fiancee: the passport cancellation warning and the NOIM 1 to 18 month window
Our Reddit thread: the at-a-glance table, with the Smartraveller and AG links

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, talk to Wedded Concierge about your date and destination.
cta_reaction.why: The checklist is solid and better sourced than most, so I trust the content. But nothing here tells me what the planner costs or whether they take a cut from suppliers. I'd bookmark the checklist and keep comparing planners.

top_3_changes: Move the early Concierge line out of the destination intro so the first pitch follows the checklist evidence, not precedes it.
Near the mid and closing CTAs, state how the fee works and whether supplier commissions or mark-ups apply, with a 'from AUD' figure once Nic signs off (deferred business detail).

Give concrete lead times where the page says 'earlier' (save-the-dates, invitations for destination guests), sourced or marked as a range, and either drop the magazine gate for the printable or say plainly what signing up involves.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ first, hunted for numbers, sources, fees and commissions
No invented brand facts; fees, commissions, Wonderland Studio and real weddings listed as deferred unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Save-the-date and invitation timing for destination guests is only 'earlier'. Is there a sourced range the writer can add, or should it stay qualitative?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for '12 month wedding checklist' while comparing planners.
Business details (fees, commissions, real weddings, Wonderland Studio) are deferred; voiced as unanswered questions only.
Link text quoted as rendered, without markdown syntax or HTML comments.
Fast-mode read: FAQ, key takeaways, destination tracks and CTAs read closely; core checklist bullets skimmed.
